findings.title: 1. [High] The `x-vercel-isr: 1` gate re-opens the unauthenticated path override that #15959 closed
findings.quote:
### 1. [High] The `x-vercel-isr: 1` gate re-opens the unauthenticated path override that #15959 closed

**File:** `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts`, lines 21–26.

**Evidence traced.**

- The new branch (`else if (request.headers.get('x-vercel-isr') === '1') realPath = url.searchParams.get(ASTRO_PATH_PARAM)`) trusts a plain request header that carries no secret. Unlike the sibling branch, which requires `x-astro-middleware-secret` to equal the per-build `crypto.randomUUID()` (`src/index.ts:261`), nothing here proves the request came from Vercel's ISR layer rather than from a client.
- The branch is not scoped to ISR. The same entrypoint is bundled into `_render` and `_isr`, and the check does not look at which function is running, at `url.pathname`, or at whether `isr` is enabled in the adapter config. So every Vercel deployment — including the majority that never enable ISR and therefore never receive a legitimate `x_astro_path` — gets the override channel back.
- The value of `x_astro_path` is not bound to the route Vercel matched. Any on-demand route can be named, including routes listed in `isr.exclude`, `/_image`, `/_server-islands/*` and API routes.
- In-process reproduction against the built handlers at the head SHA (scratch script, fixtures built by the adapter's own tests):

  | Function (fixture) | Request | Result |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `_render` (`serverless-with-dynamic-routes`, no ISR) | `GET /api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` | `{"id":"public"}` — the case #15959's test pins |
  | `_render` (same) | same request + `x-vercel-isr: 1` | `{"id":"private"}` |
  | `_render` (same) | `GET /_render?x_astro_path=/api/private` + `x-vercel-isr: 1` | `{"id":"private"}` |
  | `_render` (`middleware-with-edge-file`, edge middleware mode) | `GET /_render?x_astro_path=/` + `x-vercel-isr: 1`, no middleware secret | 200 (404 without the header) |
  | `_isr` (`isr`) | `GET /_isr?x_astro_path=/two` + `x-vercel-isr: 1` (`/two` is in `isr.exclude`) | 200, page "Two" |
  | `_isr` (`isr`) | `GET /_isr?x_astro_path=/excluded/secret` + `x-vercel-isr: 1` (excluded) | 200, page "Dynamic" |
  | `_isr` (`isr`) | `GET /_isr?x_astro_path=/api/x` + `x-vercel-isr: 1` (excluded by regex) | 200, API response |

- `test/path-override-security.test.js` still passes (4/4 with `isr.test.js`) only because neither of its two cases sends the header; adding one header to the first case flips the asserted `public` to `private`.

**Failure / vulnerability.** #15959 exists because a client-controlled path override lets the function render a different route from the one the platform matched, so anything in front of the function that decides by request path (Vercel Firewall/WAF path rules, `vercel.json`/routing-level rules, the deprecated `vercel-edge-middleware` handler, the `isr.exclude` list) is evaluated against one path while the app serves another. This PR restores that primitive behind a check that an attacker can satisfy in two ways:

1. *ISR-enabled deployments — does not depend on spoofing.* `/_isr` is a directly addressable function (`functions/_isr.func`, and the generated `config.json` contains `handle: filesystem`), with `allowQuery: ['x_astro_path']` and `passQuery: true` (`src/index.ts:709-714`). A client can request `/_isr?x_astro_path=/any/on-demand/route` itself; the platform's ISR layer then invokes the function and — by the PR's own premise that ISR invocations carry `x-vercel-isr: 1` — marks the request as trusted. The path the firewall saw was `/_isr`; the route rendered (and then cached by ISR for `expiration` seconds, even for routes the site owner excluded from ISR precisely so they are never cached) is the attacker's choice.
2. *All deployments, if the platform does not strip a client-sent `x-vercel-isr`.* Then `GET /<any routed path>?x_astro_path=/target` or `GET /_render?x_astro_path=/target` with the header is the full pre-#15959 bypass again, ISR enabled or not. I could not verify Vercel's handling of this header (the platform is unavailable to this review, and the header is undocumented — it appears nowhere else in the repository or in the installed `@vercel/*` packages); other `x-vercel-*` request headers are client-settable by design (e.g. `x-vercel-protection-bypass`), so stripping should not be assumed. The PR gives no evidence either way.

Scope note, so the severity is not overstated: Astro's own `onRequest` middleware still runs inside the function against the rewritten path in every mode I tested (in the edge-mode fixture the `_render` response carried the middleware's `x-message` and `Set-Cookie`), so authorization done in Astro middleware or in the page itself is not bypassed. The exposure is path-based controls outside the function, plus forced ISR caching of excluded routes. That is the same exposure #15959 was merged to remove.

**Direction (not applied).** Restoring ISR necessarily means trusting `x_astro_path` for genuine ISR invocations, but the trust can be made much narrower than "any request with this header, in either function, in every deployment": only honour the param in the `_isr` function (e.g. `url.pathname === '/_isr'`, or a build-time flag via `virtual:astro-vercel:config` that is false when `isr` is off) so `_render` and non-ISR deployments keep #15959's guarantee; refuse values that resolve to routes the build did not send to ISR (excluded routes, `/_image`, `/_server-islands`); and consider a route ahead of `handle: filesystem` that rejects direct client requests to `/_isr` (and `/_render`). Extend `path-override-security.test.js` with the header-bearing cases above.

findings.title: 2. [Low] No test covers the branch this PR adds, which is how the regression it fixes went unnoticed
findings.quote:
### 2. [Low] No test covers the branch this PR adds, which is how the regression it fixes went unnoticed

**File:** `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts`, lines 21–26 (no test file changed; `packages/integrations/vercel/test/isr.test.js` only asserts generated config).

**Evidence traced.** `test/isr.test.js` checks `_isr.prerender-config.json` and the route table but never calls the `_isr` handler, so #15959 could delete the param handling and stay green; this PR restores it without adding a case, and the PR body states "No additional test cases added" (manual check on a personal Vercel project only). The handler is trivially callable in-process — `test/path-override-security.test.js` already does this for `_render`, and my scratch probe did it for `_isr` (`GET https://example.com/_isr?x_astro_path=/one` with `x-vercel-isr: 1` → 200 "One"; without the header → 404).

**Failure.** The next change to this trust logic (including any tightening made in response to finding 1) can silently re-break all ISR routes with a 404, or silently widen the override, with the suite still passing.

questions.title: Q1. Is `x-vercel-isr: 1` present on every invocation of the `_isr` function, not only cached-GET regeneration?
questions.quote:
### Q1. Is `x-vercel-isr: 1` present on every invocation of the `_isr` function, not only cached-GET regeneration?

**File:** `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts`, line 24.

In ISR mode every non-prerendered route except `/_image`, `/_server-islands/*` and explicit exclusions is rewritten to `/_isr?x_astro_path=$0` (`src/index.ts:486-494`) — that includes API endpoints and Astro Actions, which receive POSTs, and it includes on-demand revalidation (`x-prerender-revalidate` with the `bypassToken`). The PR's manual test covers a plain GET of one page. If Vercel omits the header on non-GET requests or on bypass/revalidation requests to a prerender function, those requests still see pathname `/_isr`, match no route and return 404 — the bug this PR is fixing — whereas before #15959 they worked because the param was honoured unconditionally. I could not check this without the platform.

questions.title: Q2. Does Vercel's edge strip a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` request header?
questions.quote:
### Q2. Does Vercel's edge strip a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` request header?

**File:** `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts`, line 24.

This decides whether vector 2 of finding 1 is live for non-ISR deployments. A link to Vercel documentation (or a test against a deployment: `curl -H 'x-vercel-isr: 1' 'https://<deployment>/<route>?x_astro_path=/<other-route>'`) belongs in the PR, and ideally in a code comment next to the check.
